title: Model-specific runtime optimizations: Llama/Mistral/Qwen quirks + GQA/MQA tuning
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: We observed model-specific performance cliffs for recent open models (Llama family rotary edge cases, Mistral groupnorm/attention ordering, and Qwen attention tensor layout) when using the generic kernel selection and KV-cache layout. Additionally, GQA/MQA quantized variants were not landing on optimal GEMM/attention kernels for mid-length sequences (64-512), causing 10-30% latency regressions in real workloads. This PR introduces targeted heuristics, kernel variants, and KV-cache layout changes to address those quirks and a set of scheduler/batching tweaks to improve continuous-batching efficiency while preserving low tail latency for short requests.

Summary of changes (high-level): Adds model-specific kernel selection heuristics and tuned kernels for GQA/MQA; introduces a new fused attention variant for MQA that reduces memory traffic for 4-bit grouped quantization; aligns KV cache pages to 128B for improved memcpy throughput on Ampere+; improves batching scheduler with padding-aware batch formation and KV-prefetch for hot cache entries; fixes Llama rotary masking for odd-length sequences when using cached past-key/values; adds Mistral attention ordering fallback when groupnorm pre-layer behavior is detected at runtime.

Commits: "kernel: add gqa_mqa kernel selector heuristics"; "attention: fused_mqa_attention kernel (cu) + tests"; "kv_cache: 128B alignment + faster memcpy path"; "batching: padding-aware scheduler + kv-prefetch"; "llama: rotary masking fix for cached sequences"; "mistral: attention-ordering fallback"; "perf: add perf benchmarks and CI checks"; "tests: add model-specific regression tests and microbench harness".

Files changed (high-level): runtime/kernel_selector.cc, runtime/attention/fused_attention_mqa.cu, runtime/attention/fused_attention_gqa.cu, runtime/kv_cache/layout.h, runtime/kv_cache/fast_memcpy.cc, runtime/batching/scheduler.cc, runtime/batching/padding_tracker.h, runtime/model_signatures/model_hints.cc, tests/perf/bench_mqa.py, tests/regressions/llama_rotary_cached.py, docs/perf/README.md, scripts/ci/perf_matrix.yml.

Detailed notes:
- Kernel selection: Introduced a lightweight runtime model-hint mechanism (model_signatures/model_hints.cc) so the selector can prefer fused attention/GEMM kernels for known layouts (Qwen's 3D-attention layout, Mistral's pre-layer normalization pattern). The selector still falls back to the generic path if an ABI mismatch is detected. This is conservative: we only prefer specialized kernels when the model ID and weight layout checks pass.

- GQA/MQA tuning: Added a fused_mqa_attention kernel that uses blocked GEMM with 128x64 tiles, interleaved load/store, and quant-dequant paths optimized for grouped 4-bit layouts. For GQA we tuned GEMM block sizes and thread mappings to improve occupancy on A100/RTX6000-class GPUs. Microbenchmarks show ~18% throughput improvement on Qwen-type models for tokens > 128 and ~12% improvement in end-to-end latency for typical chat sequences (median length 96).

- KV cache layout: Changed in-memory KV layout to 128B-aligned pages and add a fast memcpy path that uses aligned vector loads/stores for contiguous ranges. This reduces memcpy overhead when prefetching batched KV for continuous batching and improves L2/L1 read throughput. Benchmarks indicate a 20-35% reduction in KV copy time for large past lengths (>2048 tokens).

- Llama rotary fix: There was an edge-case where cached rotary positions for odd-length prefix + current tokens produced incorrect rotation when the cached past was used across heterogeneous requests. Fixed rotation index computation and added regression tests (tests/regressions/llama_rotary_cached.py) reproducing the bug.

- Mistral fallback: Mistral variants with pre-layer groupnorm require a different attention ordering (query-key interleave). We detect the pattern via model hints and either select the specialized kernel or fall back to the stable generic attention path when pattern detection fails.

- Batching and scheduling: Implemented padding-aware batch formation: short requests that would otherwise be padded up to long-sequence shapes are grouped to preserve latency. Added a KV-prefetch hint for hot cache entries (requests that share recent prefixes) so the scheduler will prefetch contiguous KV pages asynchronously. Introduced a small scheduler heuristic to prioritize short low-token requests to meet tail-latency SLOs during high load.

Testing and CI: Added microbenchmarks and regression tests to CI perf matrix (scripts/ci/perf_matrix.yml). Initial CI run showed a flaky test in tests/perf/bench_mqa.py due to a nondeterministic GPU scheduling order; we added a deterministic seed and re-ran. Full CI: build (pass), unit tests (pass), perf-micro (pass after rerun), lint (pass).

Review conversation (high level): Daniel: requested stronger guardrails in kernel selector to avoid ABI mismatch and asked for a feature-flag gate for MQA fused kernel. Action: added conservative checks and an env var (REDWOOD_ENABLE_MQA_FUSED=1) to enable the new kernel explicitly; default off for older deployments. Sofia: asked for perf numbers and added benchmarks; asked to include a release note. Liam: approved after CI green and added a small comment about KV alignment on older hw; we added fallback to old memcpy path when alignment not supported.

Performance results (representative): Qwen-type model, seq_len=256, batch=8: end-to-end latency down 15%, tokens/sec up 18%. Llama-7B, mixed workloads with cached past up to 2048 tokens: KV copy time down 30% and tail latency (95th) down 12% when scheduling heuristics enabled. Mistral inference: stable throughput with the fallback enabled; specialized path gives ~8% throughput gain when detected.

Backward compatibility and rollout: Changes are backward compatible; all specialized kernels are behind runtime detection and a feature flag for MQA fused kernel. Provided migration notes in docs/perf/README.md. Operators can enable the MQA fused kernel via REDWOOD_ENABLE_MQA_FUSED for canary clusters before broader rollout.

Release notes: "Performance: model-specific kernel and KV-cache optimizations for Llama/Mistral/Qwen; GQA/MQA tuning reduces latency for 4-bit grouped quantized variants; batching scheduler and KV-prefetch improves continuous-batching efficiency. Includes safety gates and feature flag for MQA fused kernel."

Known limitations: The MQA fused kernel currently targets Turing/Ampere+ architectures and is disabled on older GPUs; we will add additional fallbacks for pre-Ampere when needed. Some long-sequence pathological patterns still prefer the generic kernel.
